issue.title: render_slot double-escapes already-escaped parent content since #2379, and is the framework-reachable half of the custom-tag XSS

pullRequest.title: fix(components): render_slot emits the parent's rendered slot LIVE, and a bare context string ESCAPED (#2421)

task: render_slot double-escapes already-escaped parent content since #2379, and is the framework-reachable half of the custom-tag XSS Two findings on the same handler, from the post-drain security classification. One is a **release blocker on `main`**; the other raises the severity of a shipped vulnerability. They are opposite directions on the same code path, which is why they belong together. ## 1. REGRESSION on `main` (blocker for the 1.2 RC) `{% render_slot %}` now escapes legitimate, already-escaped slot markup: ``` {% render_slot p %} p = {"content": "rendered"} v1.1.0 rendered main <strong>rendered</strong> ``` Reproduced on a release build (`make build`) after `rust_handlers.register_with_rust_engine()`. `RenderSlotTagHandler._render_value` returns `str(value.get("content", ""))` — a plain `str`. #2379 made a plain-`str` return from a tag handler get escaped, which is correct in general and wrong here: this handler's own docstring says the content is *"returned verbatim (already-escaped HTML from the parent)"*. #2379 enumerated 221 handlers and marked six as returning markup; `render_slot` was not among them. **Every function component and named slot renders its markup as visible text.** `test_named_slots.py` and `test_function_components.py` are green on both builds (32 passed each), so the suites do not cover it. ## 2. The same handler is why #2379 is framework-reachable on shipped releases `render_slot` is the **one** handler of all 221 that echoes a *context* value unescaped, so on 1.0.0 / 1.0.8 / 1.1.0: ``` {% render_slot p %} p = "" -> LIVE ``` with **no `|safe`, no `mark_safe`, and no app-written handler** — using component slots is enough. The custom-tag XSS is therefore not "if you register a handler", it is "if you use slots". This is now the joint-highest-severity item in the advisory. ## The fix must distinguish the two paths — a blanket `mark_safe` reintroduces the XSS They are genuinely different inputs and only one is trusted: - `value.get("content")` — the parent's rendered nodelist. Already escaped. Must emit raw. - a bare `str` straight from context (`p = ""`). Untrusted. Must stay escaped. `_render_value`'s trailing `return str(value)` covers the second. Marking the whole return safe would restore the shipped vulnerability; escaping both is today's regression. Mark at the one exit that is genuinely already-escaped, per #1104 (mark at one exit, not N returns). ## What a fix needs - a test that a component slot's markup renders **live**, which nothing currently asserts — this is why the regression shipped - a test that a bare hostile string through `render_slot` stays **escaped**, gated off so it reddens if the mark is widened - check `SlotTagHandler` and `CallTagHandler` for the same shape; they were in the same #2379 sweep and share the content-passing contract
